query: meta-agent modifies training environment during multi-turn reinforcement learning
text:
1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16523v1)** — October 2026. The closest match: a meta-agent monitors multi-turn RL training and modifies the environment, user simulator, rewards, and training configuration. Validated changes are applied during the ongoing run. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta); Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore); Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology); Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher); Xi Ye (University of Alberta and Amii).

2. **[Weak-for-Strong: Training Weak Meta-Agent to Harness Strong Executors](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.04785v1)** — April 2025. Related work that trains a smaller meta-agent through multi-turn RL to generate and refine workflows for stronger models. Its focus is workflow optimization, rather than modifying a live training environment. **People:** Fan Nie, Haotian Ye, Weixin Liang, Pan Lu, and James Zou (Stanford University); Lan Feng and Alexandre Alahi (EPFL); Huaxiu Yao (UNC–Chapel Hill).

query: adaptive user simulator reward design LLM agents
text:
1. **[Training Proactive and Personalized LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.02208)** (2025). Introduces **UserVille**, with preference-aware simulated users, and rewards for task success, useful clarification, and personalization. **People:** Weiwei Sun, Xuhui Zhou, Weihua Du, Sean Welleck, Graham Neubig, Maarten Sap, and Yiming Yang (Carnegie Mellon University); Xingyao Wang (OpenHands).

2. **[Learning User Simulators with Turing Rewards](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19336)** (2026). Trains user simulators using an LLM judge’s assessment of whether responses resemble a particular human’s behavior; directly relevant to simulator reward design. **People:** Yingshan Susan Wang, Cedegao E. Zhang, Linlu Qiu, Zexue He, Pengyuan Li, Alex Pentland, Roger P. Levy, and Yoon Kim. **Affiliations:** MIT, Stanford University, and MIT–IBM Watson AI Lab.

3. **[SalesSim: Benchmarking and Aligning Multimodal Language Models as Retail User Simulators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.08334)** (2026). Proposes **UserGRPO**, combining rewards for persona-consistent decisions, reasoning quality, and human-like language. **People:** Yada Pruksachatkun and Chien-Sheng Wu (Salesforce Research); Elaine Wan, Lyanna Chen, and Kai-Wei Chang (UCLA).

4. **[Towards Fast Domain Adaptation and Fine-Grained User Simulation for Evaluating Conversational Recommender Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.22803)** (2026). Introduces **AdaptSim**, which adapts simulator prompts through interaction feedback and controls user behavior and language style. **People:** Yuanzi Li, Xueyang Feng, Zihang Tian, Junhao Wang, and Xu Chen (Renmin University of China); Quanyu Dai, Zhenhua Dong, and Huifeng Guo (Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab).

query: within-run and across-run adaptation agent training
text:
1. **[A-SR: Self-Evolving Agentic LLMs for Symbolic Regression via Hierarchical Coordination](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.04872v2)** — The closest match: explicitly combines **within-run adaptation** of agent coordination and memory with **across-run training** through trajectory distillation. **People:** Wenxiao Zhao, Dong Liu, Kaiyi Xu, Feng Liu, Zhen Zhao, Fei Ben, Shu Wang, Wenhao Li, Ying Nian Wu, Fenghua Ling, Haobo Li, and Lei Bai. **Affiliations:** Shanghai AI Laboratory, UCLA, and Tongji University.

2. **[Continual Harness: Online Adaptation for Self-Improving Foundation Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.09998v1)** — Studies adaptation during a single continuous run, including joint updates to model weights and the agent’s tools, memory, and scaffolding. **People:** Seth Karten, Joel Zhang, Tersoo Upaa Jr, Ruirong Feng, Wenzhe Li, Chengshuai Shi, Chi Jin, and Kiran Vodrahalli. **Affiliations:** Princeton University, Google DeepMind, and ARISE Foundation.

3. **[ASCENT: Online Test-Time Training of Long-Horizon Agents via Self-Distillation of Verified Experience](https://artificer-ai-lab.github.io/ASCENT/)** — Particularly relevant to adaptation across tasks: verified agent trajectories produce persistent weight updates that improve subsequent attempts. Explicitly discusses the distinction from methods that adapt within an episode and reset afterward. **People:** Haodong Lu and Dong Gong. **Affiliations:** Artificer AI Lab, University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney).

2. **[Learning to Build the Environment: Self-Evolving Reasoning RL via Verifiable Environment Synthesis](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.14392v1)** — May 2026. 3. **[Agent-World: Scaling Real-World Environment Synthesis for Evolving General Agent Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.18292v1)** — April 2026. Synthesizes tool environments and adapts tasks to emerging agent capability gaps. **People:** Guanting Dong, Junting Lu, Junjie Huang, Wanjun Zhong, and collaborators, including Zhicheng Dou; the paper lists **Renmin University of China and ByteDance Seed** as participating institutions.

4. **[GenEnv: Difficulty-Aligned Co-Evolution Between LLM Agents and Environment Simulators](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.19682v1)** — December 2025. Jointly trains an agent and a simulator that generates tasks matched to the agent’s current ability. **People:** Jiacheng Guo, Jiahao Qiu, and Mengdi Wang (Princeton); Ling Yang (Princeton and ByteDance Seed); Peter Chen (Columbia); Qixin Xiao and Xinzhe Juan (University of Michigan); Yinjie Wang (University of Chicago); Ke Shen (ByteDance Seed).

2. **[SEAL: Synergistic Co-Evolution of Agents and Learning Environments](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24426)** — Uses failures from policy rollouts to jointly improve the agent and its environment’s tool guidance and feedback. **People:** Yihao Hu, Zhihao Wen, Xiujin Liu, Pan Wang, Xin Zhang, and Wei Wu. **Affiliations represented:** Ant Group, Westlake University, University of Michigan–Ann Arbor, and University of Science and Technology of China.

4. **[CoMap: Co-Evolving World Models and Agent Policies for LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.02372)** — Related approach: the agent’s world model adapts to its evolving policy through on-policy interaction. **People:** Youwei Liu (Central South University), Jian Wang (Sichuan University), and Hanlin Wang and Wenjie Li (Hong Kong Polytechnic University).

query: multi-turn reinforcement learning user simulation benchmarks
text:
1. **[LMRL Gym: Benchmarks for Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning with Language Models](https://lmrl-gym.github.io/)** — Eight multi-turn tasks, including conversations with LLM-simulated humans; provides online simulators, offline datasets, and RL baselines. **People:** Marwa Abdulhai, Isadora White, Charlie Snell, Charles Sun, Joey Hong, Yuexiang Zhai (UC Berkeley); Kelvin Xu (Google DeepMind); Sergey Levine (UC Berkeley and Google DeepMind).

2. **[τ²-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment](https://arxiv.org/html/2506.07982v1)** — Tests agents interacting with simulated users who can also operate tools, making communication and coordination essential. **People:** Victor Barres, Soham Ray, Karthik Narasimhan (Sierra); Honghua Dong (Sierra, University of Toronto, Vector Institute); Xujie Si (University of Toronto, Vector Institute).

3. **[τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.12045v1)** — Foundational benchmark for multi-turn conversations with simulated users in retail and airline scenarios, evaluating task completion and policy compliance. **People:** Shunyu Yao, Noah Shinn, Pedram Razavi, Karthik Narasimhan (Sierra; Yao’s work performed during an internship).

4. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://lifelongagent.github.io/Project-Lifelong-Agent/UserRL/index.html)** — Combines simulated users with RL training and eight evaluation environments built on UserBench; studies user feedback and reward design. **People:** Cheng Qian and Heng Ji (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, Zhiwei Liu, Haolin Chen, Shirley Kokane, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Huan Wang (Salesforce AI Research).

5. **[MUA-RL: Multi-turn User-interacting Agent Reinforcement Learning for Agentic Tool Use](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.18669v1)** — A training framework incorporating simulated users into RL rollouts, evaluated on τ-bench, τ²-Bench, BFCL-V3 Multi Turn, and ACEBench Agent. **People:** Weikang Zhao (Meituan and Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences); Xili Wang (Meituan and Peking University); Chengdi Ma (Peking University); Lingbin Kong, Zhaohua Yang, Mingxiang Tuo, Xiaowei Shi, Yitao Zhai, Xunliang Cai (Meituan).

query: methods improving user-centric agents with simulated users
text:
1. **[EAU: Environment-Agent-User Co-evolution for Training User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.16523v1)** (2026). A meta-agent improves training by diagnosing failures and adapting simulated users, environments, rewards, and RL settings. **People:** Min Cai (University of Alberta), Dan Zhang (National University of Singapore), Gao Xing and Libin Ma (Kuaishou Technology), Zhaohui Xu (independent researcher), and Xi Ye (University of Alberta / Amii).

2. **[UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning](https://lifelongagent.github.io/Project-Lifelong-Agent/UserRL/index.html)** (2025). 3. **[Beyond Cooperative Simulators: Generating Realistic User Personas for Robust Evaluation of LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.12894v1)** (2026). Evolves diverse simulated-user personas; training on these interactions improves robustness to challenging user behavior. **People:** Harshita Chopra, Kshitish Ghate, Aylin Caliskan, Chirag Shah, and Natasha Jaques (University of Washington); Tadayoshi Kohno (Georgetown University).

4. **[UserBench: An Interactive Gym Environment for User-Centric Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.22034)** (2025). A foundational evaluation environment where simulated users gradually reveal preferences, testing agents’ clarification and intent-understanding abilities. **People:** Cheng Qian (Salesforce AI Research / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign), Heng Ji (UIUC), and Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, and colleagues (Salesforce AI Research).
